why: The chat list (names replaced; status lines kept only where they are Snapchat's own words, times and streaks). Snapchat offers a click on each part of a row (avatar, name, status, Camera Reply) but on no row itself: each row becomes one item named by the chat, its status as the detail line, and the parts that are not text are left out. The filter buttons above the list (Unread, Groups, Streaks...) are left out, the header's "Chat" is the title, and Search, Notification and Add Friends go to the options. Its title sits in the middle of its own top bar, so in the middle of Relaid's.
title: Chat

why: A chat. Snapchat offers a click on every message and on who wrote it: the senders (ME, TEAM SNAPCHAT) become headings and the messages text, the title is the chat's name, and the field sends with Enter. Camera, voice note, Stickers, Memories and Games are left out: none of them works from another phone. Team Snapchat's message is the screen's body text, and the bar's own lines (its name, the line under it) are drawn at the device's own sizes.
title: Team Snapchat

why: A chat with a snap in it. A snap is a picture Relaid does not show, and opening it on the host would use it up, so it stays text; the date heads its messages.
title: Team Snapchat

why: A chat with a friend (names and texts replaced). The audio and video call buttons are left out: a call cannot work from another phone, and one tap would ring the friend. Nothing in the message list is a control. The two messages are pictures with no text: each is a picture the host captures live (pictures), labelled "Picture or video" until it arrives, the first with the app's notice about it ("You saved a Snap in Chat!") as its second line.
title: Friend One

why: A chat with a friend with text messages (names and texts replaced). Who wrote each message (FRIEND ONE, ME) is a heading above it, as are the dates; a picture's sender too; the call buttons are left out.
title: Friend One
